headline: Head Start Plans $7.2 Million for Micronesia and Marshall Islands
dek: Two proposed sole-source awards would support early-childhood services over 60 months, with $3.6 million designated for each freely associated state.

sources.title: Announcement of the Intent To Award Sole-Source Awards to the Federated States of Micronesia and the Republic of the Marshall Islands

lead.creator: U.S. Navy
lead.rightsBasis: The official U.S. Navy documentary photograph is identified as public domain on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.caption: U.S. Navy Seabees work on the roof of Kolonia Elementary School in Pohnpei during Pacific Partnership 2025. The school project is separate from the proposed Head Start awards.
lead.alt: Construction workers repair the roof of a school building in Pohnpei.

charts.caption: The Office of Head Start proposes up to $3.6 million each for Micronesia and the Marshall Islands, $7.2 million in total.
charts.alt: Graphic shows two awards of 3.6 million dollars, totaling 7.2 million dollars.

charts.caption: The proposed project period is 60 months, beginning with 12 months of funding and possible annual supplements.
charts.alt: Graphic shows a 60-month project period, an initial 12-month award and possible annual supplements.

paragraphs: The Office of Head Start intends to award up to $7.2 million to establish early-childhood services in the Federated States of Micronesia and the Republic of the Marshall Islands.

The Aug. 12 notice proposes two sole-source grants of up to $3.6 million each. The grants would support Early Head Start, Head Start Preschool or a combination of the two; the notice does not yet identify enrollment totals or opening dates.

The proposed performance period is 60 months, subject to available funds. The agency plans an initial 12-month award followed by yearly supplements that depend on funding, satisfactory performance and compliance with federal requirements.

Congress provided $8 million in fiscal 2026 appropriations to extend Head Start eligibility and services in the Freely Associated States. The two awards announced in this notice total up to $7.2 million; the notice does not allocate the remaining appropriation.

Programs could provide early education, health, nutrition and family-support services while building local operating capacity. The two governments, or entities they designate, would plan and run the services.

The agency says the national governments are the only jurisdictions eligible for these funds under the new authority and their Compacts of Free Association with the United States. That statutory structure is the stated basis for using sole-source awards.

For the first 24 months, the recipients would be exempt from the Head Start Designation Renewal System's competition requirements. After that period, competition can be triggered if one or more conditions in that system are met.
The notice announces an intent rather than a completed award. Final amounts, annual supplements and the pace of service expansion remain contingent on funding, performance and grant administration.
facts: Two proposed awards total up to $7.2 million.
Each proposed award is up to $3.6 million.
The proposed project period is 60 months.
The first 24 months are exempt from designation-renewal competition requirements.
uncertainty: The notice does not give enrollment targets or program opening dates.
Funding beyond the first 12 months depends on appropriations, performance and compliance.
seoTitle: Head Start plans $7.2M for Micronesia and Marshall Islands
seoDescription: Head Start proposes two $3.6 million sole-source awards for early-childhood services in Micronesia and the Marshall Islands over 60 months.

headline: FAA Sets Display Rules for Skyryse Fly-by-Wire R66
dek: The final special conditions require clear mode, control-position and system-state information when digital controls replace mechanical feedback in the helicopter.

sources.title: Special Conditions: Skyryse, Robinson Helicopter Company Model R66 Helicopter; Flight Control System Annunciation of Control

lead.creator: Jubair1985
lead.rightsBasis: The photographer licensed the documentary Robinson R66 photograph CC BY-SA 4.0 on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.caption: A Robinson R66 helicopter photographed in 2017. FAA's special conditions apply to an R66 modified by Skyryse with digital fly-by-wire controls.
lead.alt: Robinson R66 helicopter parked on an airfield apron.

charts.caption: The R66 certification basis covers a 2,700-pound maximum takeoff weight, up to five passengers and single-pilot day or night VFR operations.
charts.alt: Graphic lists 2,700 pounds, five passengers and single-pilot visual flight rules operations.

charts.caption: FAA requires the pilot display to identify the current mode, commanded control positions and relevant fly-by-wire system state and alerts.
charts.alt: Graphic lists current mode, commanded positions, system state and alerts as required pilot information.

paragraphs: The Federal Aviation Administration has issued final display requirements for a Skyryse digital flight-control conversion of the Robinson R66 helicopter.

Skyryse proposes replacing the R66's mechanical primary controls with a fly-by-wire system called SkyOS. The special conditions take effect Sept. 11 and become part of the certification basis for this specific modification.

Mechanical pushrods normally give a pilot tactile feedback through the cyclic and collective. FAA says that feedback is absent when computers calculate the commanded control positions, creating a gap in rules written for mechanical systems.

The final conditions require the system's functions, controls, indications and alerts to minimize pilot errors and confusion. They also require a visible indication of the current mode and clearly grouped information under all expected lighting conditions.

The display must communicate commanded primary-control positions and relevant information about the fly-by-wire system's operating state. Degraded functions needed for continued safe flight and landing are included in the requirement.

FAA describes the R66 as a single-engine, normal-category helicopter with a maximum takeoff weight of 2,700 pounds and seating for up to five passengers. It is approved for one pilot and day or night flight under visual flight rules.
The agency received one general objection to its proposed special conditions, but the commenter offered no explanation or requested change. FAA adopted the conditions as proposed.

The action is not an approval of every operational claim for SkyOS or a rule for all helicopters. Skyryse still must show that the modified aircraft meets the applicable certification basis before the supplemental type certificate can be issued.
facts: The special conditions take effect Sept. 11, 2026.
The modification replaces mechanical primary controls with digital fly-by-wire controls.
The R66 has a 2,700-pound maximum takeoff weight.
The display must indicate the current operating mode.
uncertainty: The special conditions do not themselves issue Skyryse a supplemental type certificate.
Any expansion to other models would require a separate application and applicable certification work.
seoTitle: FAA sets Skyryse fly-by-wire R66 display rules
seoDescription: FAA finalized pilot-display requirements for Skyryse's fly-by-wire Robinson R66 conversion, addressing the loss of mechanical control feedback.

headline: NCI Offers Checkpoint-Resistant Cancer Cell Line for Licensing
dek: The CRISPR-engineered mouse colon-cancer model removes B2m and MHC-I antigen presentation to support preclinical research on resistance to PD-1 and PD-L1 therapies.

sources.title: Government Owned Invention Available for License: MC38 B2m KO Cell Line

lead.creator: Diane A. Reid / National Cancer Institute
lead.rightsBasis: The National Cancer Institute laboratory photograph is identified as a U.S. government public-domain work on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.attribution: Diane A. Reid / National Cancer Institute, public domain
lead.caption: A National Institutes of Health laboratory in a National Cancer Institute photograph. The agency is seeking licensees for a new preclinical cancer research tool.
lead.alt: Researcher working at a laboratory bench with scientific equipment.

charts.caption: CRISPR deletion of B2m removes MHC-I antigen presentation, limiting a key signal used by cancer-killing CD8-positive T cells.
charts.alt: Graphic links B2m deletion to loss of MHC-I antigen presentation and reduced T-cell recognition.

charts.caption: NCI describes the knockout tumors as resistant to anti-PD-1 and anti-PD-L1 treatment while wild-type MC38 tumors remain checkpoint-responsive.
charts.alt: Graphic contrasts checkpoint-resistant B2m knockout tumors with responsive wild-type MC38 tumors.

paragraphs: The National Cancer Institute is seeking licensees for a laboratory cell line designed to model a common route to resistance against cancer checkpoint immunotherapy.

The research tool is a CRISPR/Cas9-engineered version of the mouse MC38 colon-cancer cell line. NCI researchers deleted B2m, a gene needed for tumor cells to display major histocompatibility complex class I molecules.

MHC-I presentation helps cancer-killing CD8-positive T cells recognize tumor targets. Removing B2m takes away that immune-recognition signal and produces tumors that resist anti-PD-1 and anti-PD-L1 treatment in the agency's model.

The original MC38 line responds strongly to PD-1 and PD-L1 checkpoint blockade, NCI says. Pairing the knockout and wild-type lines can therefore support controlled comparisons between resistant and responsive tumors.

Researchers could use the model to study the biology of defective antigen presentation and test preclinical strategies aimed at checkpoint-refractory tumors. The notice also identifies work on combination immunotherapies as a potential application.

The technology is a murine preclinical research tool, not a treatment, clinical-trial result or evidence that a strategy will work in people. Findings from a mouse model require separate validation before any clinical conclusion.
NCI lists the invention under reference E-123-2026-0 and says no patents are filed. The agency is offering licenses and may consider collaboration to further develop and evaluate the tool.
Availability for licensing does not establish commercial performance or clinical benefit. Terms, research plans and any downstream regulatory pathway would be handled separately.
facts: NCI created the line with CRISPR/Cas9.
The deleted B2m gene is required for MHC-I antigen presentation.
The knockout tumors resist anti-PD-1 and anti-PD-L1 treatment in the described model.
The technology is listed as NIH reference E-123-2026-0.
uncertainty: Results from this mouse model cannot establish safety or efficacy in humans.
The notice does not identify a licensee or a commercialization timeline.
seoTitle: NCI offers MC38 B2m checkpoint-resistant cell line for licensing
seoDescription: NCI is licensing a CRISPR-engineered mouse cancer cell line that models resistance to PD-1 and PD-L1 checkpoint therapies.

headline: NOAA Diving Records Carry 336 Annual Burden Hours
dek: The agency estimates 141 respondents for medical and equipment records supporting more than 300 divers, with comments on the renewal due Oct. 13.

sources.title: Agency Information Collection Activities; NOAA Diving Program

lead.creator: D. Kesling / NOAA
lead.rightsBasis: The NOAA documentary technical-diving photograph is identified as a U.S. government public-domain work on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.caption: A NOAA technical diver works underwater. The agency is seeking comment on renewing medical, authorization and equipment records for its diving program.
lead.alt: Technical diver in full equipment working underwater beside a structure.

charts.caption: NOAA estimates 141 respondents, response times from one minute to two hours and 336 total annual burden hours.
charts.alt: Graphic shows 141 respondents, one minute to two hours per response and 336 annual burden hours.

charts.caption: Estimated annual public cost ranges from about $1,750 if every respondent has private insurance to an $11,700 upper bound without it.
charts.alt: Graphic shows annual public cost estimates from 1,750 dollars to an upper bound of 11,700 dollars.

paragraphs: NOAA is seeking comment on renewing the records it uses to qualify, authorize and equip participants in its diving program.

The agency says it has more than 300 divers, the largest diving complement of any civilian federal agency. The group includes NOAA employees as well as contractors, volunteers and others who conduct agency operations.

Divers support scientific research and operational work in conditions ranging from warm marine sanctuaries to cold, low-visibility commercial harbors. Most support the National Ocean Service, National Marine Fisheries Service or Office of Marine and Aviation Operations.

NOAA requires candidates to submit a diving physical and authorized divers to provide annual medical documentation. Scheduled equipment maintenance and continuing proficiency requirements also affect authorization.
For the information collection, NOAA estimates 141 respondents and 336 total annual burden hours. Depending on the instrument, a response can take from one minute to two hours.

The agency sets $11,700 as an upper-bound annual public cost if respondents obtaining medical examinations lack private insurance. If all have private insurance and a $35 copay, NOAA estimates about $1,750.
Information is collected electronically by email, and responding is required to obtain or retain program benefits. These are paperwork estimates, not the full cost of operating NOAA's diving program.
Comments are due Oct. 13. NOAA is asking whether the collection is necessary, whether its estimates are accurate and how it can improve quality or reduce reporting burden.
facts: NOAA reports more than 300 divers.
The collection estimates 141 respondents.
Estimated annual burden is 336 hours.
The upper-bound estimated annual public cost is $11,700.
uncertainty: Actual medical costs depend on respondents' insurance coverage.
The renewal notice does not set the number of dives or projects NOAA will conduct.
seoTitle: NOAA diving records estimate 336 annual burden hours
seoDescription: NOAA estimates 141 respondents and 336 annual hours for its diving-program records, with public costs ranging from about $1,750 to $11,700.

headline: Puerto Rico U.S. Attorney Plans Community Outreach Request Form
dek: Schools, nonprofits, municipalities and community groups could request educational presentations through a voluntary form estimated at 10 minutes per response.
entities: U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Puerto Rico

sources.title: USAO-PR Community Outreach Request Form Feedback Form Package
sources.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Puerto Rico

lead.creator: Andrea Booher / FEMA
lead.rightsBasis: The official FEMA documentary photograph is identified as a U.S. government public-domain work on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.caption: A FEMA community-relations team meets outdoors in Puerto Rico in an agency photograph. The scene illustrates federal community outreach and does not depict the U.S. Attorney's proposed form.
lead.alt: Federal community-relations staff hold an outdoor meeting in Puerto Rico.

charts.caption: The U.S. Attorney's Office estimates 250 voluntary responses a year, about 10 minutes each and 41.8 total burden hours.
charts.alt: Graphic shows 250 annual responses, 10 minutes per response and 41.8 burden hours.

charts.caption: Potential requesters include schools, nonprofit organizations, community groups, municipalities and other organizations.
charts.alt: Graphic lists schools, nonprofits, community groups, municipalities and other organizations.

paragraphs: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Puerto Rico plans a new form for organizations seeking educational presentations and other community outreach.
Schools, nonprofit organizations, community groups, municipalities and other organizations would be able to submit requests. Responding would be voluntary.
The office estimates 250 responses per year, about 10 minutes for each response and 41.8 total annual burden hours. It reports no capital, startup, maintenance or purchase costs for respondents.

The form would collect information needed to evaluate and coordinate presentation requests. The notice does not list a fixed catalog of presentation subjects or promise that every request will be accepted.
The office says it would use the information to allocate resources and track outreach. It also identifies community concerns, emerging crime trends and program evaluation as intended uses.
Those uses describe how the office plans to manage outreach information; they do not establish that a requester's concern reflects a verified crime trend or law-enforcement finding.

The collection is new and remains subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act process. Comments can address the need for the form, the accuracy of its burden estimate and ways to improve clarity or reduce effort.
Comments are due Oct. 13. Final form design, launch timing and the resulting schedule of outreach events remain to be determined after review.
facts: The proposed collection is new and voluntary.
The office estimates 250 respondents annually.
Estimated response time is about 10 minutes.
Estimated annual burden is 41.8 hours with $0 in other costs.
uncertainty: The notice does not give a launch date or guarantee that requests will be fulfilled.
The final form can change after public and OMB review.
seoTitle: Puerto Rico U.S. Attorney proposes community outreach request form
seoDescription: A proposed voluntary form would let Puerto Rico schools, nonprofits and municipalities request U.S. Attorney outreach presentations in about 10 minutes.

headline: IRS Estimates 30.6 Million Hours for Foreign-Status Tax Forms
dek: The agency is seeking comment on renewing five W-8 certifications used for U.S. withholding decisions, with 3.39 million respondents in its estimate.

sources.title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request on the Burden Related to Foreign Status and U.S. Withholding Certifications

lead.creator: Carol M. Highsmith
lead.rightsBasis: Carol M. Highsmith dedicated the documentary IRS headquarters photograph to the public domain through the Library of Congress.
lead.attribution: Carol M. Highsmith / Library of Congress, public domain
lead.caption: The Internal Revenue Service headquarters on Constitution Avenue in Washington. IRS is seeking comment on renewing five W-8 foreign-status certifications.
lead.alt: Exterior of the Internal Revenue Service headquarters building in Washington.

charts.caption: IRS estimates 3,390,700 respondents, an average of 9 hours and 1 minute each, and 30,562,942 total annual burden hours.
charts.alt: Graphic shows 3.39 million respondents, 9 hours and 1 minute each, and 30.56 million burden hours.

charts.caption: The renewal covers Forms W-8BEN, W-8BEN-E, W-8ECI, W-8EXP and W-8IMY under OMB control number 1545-1621.
charts.alt: Graphic lists five W-8 forms covered by the IRS information-collection renewal.

paragraphs: The Internal Revenue Service estimates that foreign-status and U.S. withholding certifications account for more than 30.5 million hours of annual paperwork burden.
IRS is seeking comment on renewing the collection covering Forms W-8BEN, W-8BEN-E, W-8ECI, W-8EXP and W-8IMY. The agency says it is making no change to the burden estimate in this review.
The forms let foreign individuals, entities, intermediaries, governments and some tax-exempt organizations certify their status for U.S. withholding and reporting purposes.

Withholding agents use those certifications to determine the applicable tax treatment, including possible reduced rates or exemptions under the Internal Revenue Code. The collection notice does not itself change anyone's tax liability.
IRS estimates 3,390,700 respondents, an average of nine hours and one minute per respondent and 30,562,942 total annual burden hours.
Those figures are Paperwork Reduction Act estimates for the entire collection. They do not mean every filer completes all five forms or spends the same amount of time.

The affected public includes businesses, individuals and nonprofit institutions. IRS is asking whether the collection has practical utility, whether its estimate is accurate and whether technology or other changes could reduce burden.
Comments are due Oct. 13. The renewal process does not provide individualized tax guidance, and the notice says public comments should omit confidential or sensitive personal information.
facts: The collection covers five W-8 forms.
IRS estimates 3,390,700 respondents.
Average estimated time is nine hours and one minute per respondent.
Estimated total annual burden is 30,562,942 hours.
uncertainty: Actual completion time varies by respondent and form.
The notice renews an existing collection and does not announce substantive tax-law changes.
seoTitle: IRS W-8 forms carry 30.6 million annual burden hours
seoDescription: IRS estimates 3.39 million respondents and 30.56 million annual hours for five foreign-status and U.S. withholding certification forms.
